brief: September NFP grew 29k, below the 35k-180k estimate range and the 90k median, with August revised down to 133k from 162k, for 60k of downward revisions over two months. The unemployment rate rose to 4.2% (estimated unchanged at 4.1%) as participation rose to 61.8% (estimated unchanged at 61.6%). Hourly earnings growth slowed. SEB argues immigration restrictions and an aging population have lowered the break-even employment growth needed for a stable labor market to 30-60k per month, so the slowdown is not necessarily weakness, and current 3-month average growth of ~50k still fits that range. This undercuts the case, built on August's strong print, that Fed policy is not restrictive enough. SEB believes the data supports Fed vice chairs John Williams and Philip Jefferson's view that the Fed could pause in October to evaluate the September hike. Markets cut the probability of an October hike to about 20% but still fully price a December hike and three more hikes total through 2026-2027. SEB keeps its own forecast: one more hike in December, then a return to rate cuts in late 2027.
